question.problem:
Consider the system of linear differential equations given by

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ -1 & -3\end{aligned}]x(t).
$$

Given that the solution to the system can be written as

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}a \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}a \\ 1\end{aligned}]t{e}^{-t}+[\begin{aligned}b \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}),\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of $a+b?$

*Hint: The only eigenvalue of the system's matrix is $\lambda =-1.$*

current_example.worked_solution:
We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14216492/assets/e3450fb9920802330b599ac3f7f1bf66bc5e26265c2aefcb87e45829abcdabcc.svg)

Since $A$ is upper-triangular, the repeated eigenvalue is $\lambda=-4$ (of multiplicity two).
For this eigenvalue, we get 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14216492/assets/3b561e7e1f9aef5dfe936e8aa2b86a57674685c85e221cc869fe0988623154c0.svg)
So, we get an eigenvector 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14216492/assets/19f2155257a5edb9602f511f3f8dd4174cb44ecef38a0deeda3a528cd278ecbf.svg)

Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda$ and only one linearly independent eigenvector $\mathbf v,$ the solution of the system of differential equations is given by

$$
\mathbf{x}(t) = c_1\mathbf{v} e^{\lambda t}  + c_2 (\mathbf{v}  te^{\lambda t}  +  \mathbf{w}e^{\lambda t} \, ),
$$

where $\mathbf{w}$ is a solution to the equation $(A - \lambda I)\mathbf{w}= \mathbf{v}.$

To find $\mathbf{w},$ we solve the equation $(A - \lambda I)\mathbf{w} = \mathbf{v}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(A-\lambda I)w & =v \\ [\begin{aligned}-4+4 & 1 \\ 0 & -4+4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The last equality allows us to form the following system of equations:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14216492/assets/880e31f45c35b76fa680b0472738e678b34da35e2638a11cdc71a401e1e201f1.svg)

So, we obtain

$$
w_2 = 1.
$$

The variable $w_1$ is a free variable. Setting $w_1 = 0,$ we get 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14216492/assets/c975c6f69ac451477af03fdeba6537f656040f1fbb5e8dcc3d78753aee7f5117.svg)

Therefore, the general solution is given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14216492/assets/2d9b1522faa5737e17627901003c1d5d739028bdf7678729f002c39c0d73594c.svg)

Finally, we see that $a=0, b=1,$ and $a+b=1.$
